subject: flying fish
title: A Flying Fish Stayed in the Air for 45 Seconds

scenes.text: This fish escapes the ocean's hunters by leaving the ocean.
Flying fish race toward the surface at about 37 miles an hour.
They burst out, spread fins like wings and glide, beating their tail on the water to keep going.
One glide can cover over 600 feet. Several in a row, over 1,300.
In 2008, a Japanese TV crew filmed one in the air for 45 seconds.
Below, tuna and dolphinfish lose the trail. Their meal just flew away.

description:
Flying fish reach about 37 mph underwater before breaking the surface, then glide on wing-like fins; a single glide can reach about 600-655 feet and a chain of glides about 1,300 feet.
In May 2008 an NHK crew filmed one airborne for 45 seconds off Kagoshima, Japan, a Guinness record.
What animal would you most like to see fly?
first_comment: Flying fish sometimes land on ship decks at night. Would you rather be the tuna or the fish?
